title: A 5 m/s reduction-difference screen flags one of four bright-twilight nights in 18 selected HARPS stars
abstract: We test a twilight artifact screen with 19 existing HARPS RVBank version 2 files. A local dark-night reference leaves 18 stars with eligible data. With quality flag zero and signal to noise above 20, only four nights in three stars have the Sun above -10 degrees. One raw DRS minus SERVAL difference is more than 5 m/s from the local dark median. The other three are below 0.6 m/s. The dark group has 151 flags in 2649 nights. Broader solar altitude cuts change the sample and the rates. Supplied corrections keep one bright-twilight flag. This small selected sample does not establish a general twilight effect or show that twilight data are safe. Both reductions use the same spectra. No new planet or physical cause is confirmed. Code, aggregate results, a figure, exact input hashes and an external retrieval recipe are included.

display.caption: Aggregate raw reduction-difference bins and target medians. Four bright-twilight nights give little precision. HD 69830 does not pass the dark-control requirement.

citations.reason: Source of the twilight hypothesis and the site/time convention. We do not reuse source code or numerical measurements.
